question: What raises a new game's technology above the history before the first screen: when it runs, for whom, against which date, whether a load runs it, and the selection rule.

addresses.name: SetUpCountryLawsAndTechnologyForNewGame
addresses.comment:
**What brings a new game's countries up to the start date: their laws first, then their technology.** VA 0x4D59D0 to the `ret 4` at 0x4D622D, read whole on the listing (FINDINGS-starttech.md); SetUpCountryForNewGame begins on the next byte with no padding. One stack argument, the country. **One caller, 0x65B4E6 in CInGameIdler::Enter**, in the per-country loop over every country of the game state (+0xBBC), inside the block that loaded_from_save (+0xD9C) == 0 guards at 0x65B4D4 - so it runs once per country as a new game is entered, before that country's LoadOobFile (0x65B4EC) and SetUpCountryForNewGame (0x65B4F2), before the two days a new game runs, never on a load, and with no test of who plays the country. No data reference to it.

**Laws** (VA 0x4D59F4-0x4D5BD7): one CEventScope, country = this one, FROM `---`. For each law group by index from 1 (GetLawDataBase +0x28), the group's law list (CLawGroup +0xC) is walked: a law whose modifier values hold a non-zero entry 52 (`[law+0x18]+0x1A0`, UNIT_START_EXPERIENCE) abandons the whole group; the current law (CCountry +0x628[i]) is noted and **no law after it in the list is asked**; a law met before it whose `allow` (CLaw +0x54, slot 6) holds becomes the country's law at once (`laws[group->index (+0x50)] = law`) - a plain store, no CChangeLawCommand, no cost, no message. Any change, and CCountry::RebuildStaticModifiers (0x4DDD80). CLawGroup::LoadKey pushes each law on the front of that list, so it runs in the reverse of laws.txt's order: a law is moved to the **latest law of its group in file order whose allow holds, if that is later than its own**, and training_laws, whose last law has unit_start_experience, is never touched. The law half was not set against a save (FINDINGS-starttech.md, *What is not established*).

**Technology** (VA 0x4D5BD7-0x4D622D). A budget: y = the year of the game's tick, m its month counted from 0; x = y x 1000 + trunc((m x 1000 - 1000) x 1000 / 12000) + 2000 - (the year of CDefines +8, start_date) x 1000 - **1917 on 1 January of the start year**; L = the sum of `leadership` (+0x324) over the country's CoreProvinces (+0xD10), owned or not, held to 5000; budget = trunc(trunc(3650 x x / 1000) x L / 1000). The 3650 and the 12000 are (int)floorf of the floats 3650.5 and 12000.5 at 0x160AA60 and 0x160A82C; the 2000, the 5000 and the doubling below are immediates. Then, while budget > 0: over the technology database (g_CTechnologyDataBase +0) in its order, skipping a technology with additional_offset 0 already at a level, one in the folder named `theory_folder` (looked up by name in the database's +0x4C map), one CTechnology::CheckResearchAllowed(tag, -1) refuses, and one whose **current** level's year (GetYear arithmetic: start_year for a level of 1 or less, first_offset for 2, + additional_offset a level above) is not before y; the price is CTechnologyStatus::GetResearchCost, **doubled when the next level's year is not before y**, and the cheapest wins, the first in database order among equals (strict `<` against a start of 99999.000). None, and it stops. Otherwise budget -= GetResearchCost / 100 (undoubled) and the level becomes min(level + 1, max_level), written straight into level_by_technology (+0x218) at 0x4D620F - no progress, no ability, no on_completion, no message, no history entry; SetUpCountryForNewGame's ReapplyAllTechnologies (0x4D7346) then rebuilds the status from the new levels. The built-in `notech`, which no file declares and which stands first in the database, is bought like any other at 125.000 (1250 of the budget). Against Germany1936_01_01_00.hoi3 this reproduces **all 476 levels the start save holds above the history, in all 86 countries that have any, and notech's level in all 101** (88 at 1, 13 at 0) - Germany 22, China 17, Germany's 36 behind left alone. The name is ours. **Why notech is bought** (reader A): LoadTechnologies builds it through the ordinary CTechnology constructor (0x5339A0, at VA 0x541407) - start_year 0, additional_offset 0, max_level 1, difficulty 0, no folder, no research_bonus_from, an empty allow - and this function never asks slot 9, the test that tells the null technology from a real one; left out of the candidates, the same loop gives one level too many in 69 countries. **It is the only writer of a level that is not research, the history, a savegame, a reset, a release or the custom game** - a census of every load of +0x218 in .text followed to a store (FINDINGS-starttech.md, section 1).
addresses.evidence: Extent: `push ebp` at 0x4D59D0 (int3 run before it, after CCountry_RevertDisallowedLaws's `ret 4` at 0x4D59BE), single `ret 4` at 0x4D622D, retsBefore(0x4D59D0, 0x4D622D) empty, SetUpCountryForNewGame at 0x4D6230. Caller: findRefs --callers 0x4D59D0 gives exactly 0x65B4E6; findValue in .text and .rdata gives none. The guard: `cmp byte ptr [ecx+0xd9c],0; jne 0x65b7c9` at 0x65B4D4 with ecx = g_CCurrentGameState. The level write: `mov dword ptr [edx+edi*4], ecx` at 0x4D620F, edx = [[country+0xdf8]+0x218], edi = [tech+0x244], ecx = min(level+1, [tech+0x2c4]) by `cmovg`. Budget: `cmp ebx,0x1388; jle` at 0x4D5EBE, `imul dword ptr [ebp-0x14]` / __alldiv 1000 / `imul ebx` / __alldiv 1000; floats 3650.5 and 12000.5 read with image.read; `mov edx,0x7d0; sub edx,eax` at 0x4D5E01 with eax = year([defines+8]) x 1000. Selection: `cmp eax,[ebp-0x38]; jge` at 0x4D60F3 (current level's year), the doubling `push 0x7d0 ... __allmul; __alldiv 1000` at 0x4D6135 behind `cmp ecx,[ebp-0x38]; jl`, `cmp eax,[ebp-0x20]; jge` at 0x4D6155 with [ebp-0x20] = 0x5F5DD18 at the top of each pass; payment cost x 1000 / 100000 (0x14F8B589 >> 45) at 0x4D61A7. Simulated over the start save (scratchpad hlB/sim.py) it predicts 476 of 476 raised levels and notech in 101 of 101; each control breaks it: x 1900 or 1930, the cap at 4900 or 5100, year 1935, no doubling, theories included, notech left out, a `<=` tie-break or the database reversed, the exact square root in place of FixedPointSqrt's (75 to 6 countries exact of 86). What would show it wrong: a new game whose raised levels the simulation does not give - a later bookmark is the untested case. The law half rests on the listing alone. Reached independently from the data by a second reader (every writer of +0x218), whose own simulation gives the same 476 lines - 627 level steps, none extra and none missed - and notech in all 101 (hlA/sim.py, NOTECH=1).

addresses.name: Enter_StartLawsAndTechnology
addresses.comment: `call SetUpCountryLawsAndTechnologyForNewGame` in CInGameIdler::Enter, the first call of the per-country block a new game runs (loaded_from_save, +0xD9C, tested at 0x65B4D4), before CCountry::LoadOobFile (0x65B4EC) and SetUpCountryForNewGame (0x65B4F2). The one place a new game's technology is raised above the history. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-starttech.md.
addresses.evidence: `mov edi,[esp+0x50]; push edi; call 0x4d59d0` at 0x65B4E1..0x65B4E6, then `push edi; call 0x4ffed0` and `push edi; call 0x4d6230`; [esp+0x50] is the country the loop at 0x65B157 took from the game state's +0xBBC vector. The only direct call to 0x4D59D0.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::Enter
addresses.comment: **What runs as a session comes up, for a new game and a loaded one alike.** Large; it walks every country of the game, and per country: UpdateTriggeredModifiers, RebuildStaticModifiers, RebuildRules, UpdateTotalLeadership, UpdateMaxManpower, UpdateIC, UpdateBlockadeLevel, UpdateAtWarAndEnemies and effective neutrality. **For a session not loaded from a save** it then calls SetUpCountryLawsAndTechnologyForNewGame (0x65B4E6 - the laws moved up and the technology bought to the start date, FINDINGS-starttech.md), reads the country's order of battle (CCountry::LoadOobFile, 0x65B4EC), calls SetUpCountryForNewGame and RecountUnitTotals, sets the shares of IC, counts the officers the units come with (0x65B651), and **sets up the build queue (0x65B749): for each line of +0xF40 it keeps the duration the file gave, calls slot 14, and sets progress to the new duration less the old, floored at 0** - so a file's `duration` is the days a line still has to go, and its `progress` and `cost` are thrown away. The arm beside it at 0x65B7C9 calls 0x4DCD70 and joins the same place; that it is a loaded session's is FINDINGS-unitstart.md's reading of the block and was not followed here. Then, for each of the country's units, what FINDINGS-unitstart.md section 6 has. The write that sets `in_game` is 0x4A92 bytes before the end. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitstart.md, section 1, and FINDINGS-buildqueue.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Adds the call at 0x65B4E6, which the comment's list of the new-game block left out: `push edi; call 0x4d59d0` between the loaded_from_save test at 0x65B4D4 and `call 0x4ffed0` at 0x65B4EC. Nothing else in the entry is changed.

addresses.name: CTechnologyStatus::ReapplyAllTechnologies
addresses.comment:
Resets the status (0x531DE0) and then calls ApplyTechnologyEffects (rva 0x132970) once per technology the country has a level in, with `scale = level x 1000` and the technology in edi. `ret 4`. **Three callers**: ApplyCustomGameSettings at 0x41DC85 (a custom game), CCountry::AfterLoad at 0x4D26B1, and SetUpCountryForNewGame at 0x4D7346 - the last is what carries a new game's start technology (SetUpCountryLawsAndTechnologyForNewGame, which writes the levels and nothing else) into unit figures, activated units and buildings. This said ApplyCustomGameSettings alone until 2026-11-02.

**Watch the extent**: `image.functionStart(0x532943)` answers 0x532940, which is inside this function's loop - the two do not abut, the helper simply scans back to the wrong place. The name is BiceLib's.
addresses.evidence: findRefs --callers 0x532840: exactly 0x41DC85, 0x4D26B1 and 0x4D7346; functionStart(0x4D26B1) = 0x4D2500 with retsBefore empty, which the record names CCountry::AfterLoad; 0x4D7346 is inside SetUpCountryForNewGame (0x4D6230..0x4D757A), whose own comment already lists the call.

struct_fields.name: espionage
struct_fields.comment: the first of an array of 0xF8 byte entries, one per country, ending at +0x1164. **Entry +0 is what the save writes as `spy_allocation`** - CCountry::LoadKey's case for that key (0xCE3C1) walks the array 0xF8 at a time writing entry+0 - and entry+4 is `spy_priority` (0xCE34B writes `[edx + esi + 4]`), entry+0xF4 `covert_ops_points`; `spy_mission` walks nine values an entry. The country's `spies` key is **not** in here: it is a single field elsewhere on the country. Entry+0 is thousandths - an accessor at 0x49F3B0 answers `< 1000`, i.e. under one spy, and everything that writes it clamps to the 10000 at rva 0x130D164. CModifySpiesEffect::Execute adds to entry+0, which is what that effect is for: the spies this country has on mission in the target. The country's `spies` field at +0x1170 is a separate figure. **A new game's first entry+0 is SetUpCountryForNewGame's** (its relations loop, VA 0x4D710E..0x4D733F): from relations and faction, and only for a session not loaded from a save. This comment said until 2026-11-02 that 'the assigner at 0xD59D0' recomputes it whenever a game is entered, so that a value written mid-game does not survive a reload; 0xD59D0 is SetUpCountryLawsAndTechnologyForNewGame, which touches laws and technology and never the espionage array, and the address came from a walk back that crosses the unpadded boundary at 0x4D622D (trap 2). Whether anything rewrites entry+0 on a load was not looked for.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x4D59D0..0x4D622D read whole: no access to +0x1160 (its reads of the country are +0x628, +0xCA4, +0xCA8, +0xD10, +0xDF8). The spy allocation store is in SetUpCountryForNewGame's relations loop, which that entry already records. The 0xD59D0 attribution is most likely a walk back over the unpadded `ret 4` at 0x4D622D, which SetUpCountryForNewGame's own comment says fieldchain.py makes; the field's source is a BiceLib header, so how it was derived was not checked.

struct_fields.name: laws
struct_fields.comment: Head of the group's list of its laws: a node is {CLaw*, next} with next at node+4. CCountry_RevertDisallowedLaws walks it in order and takes the first law whose allow holds, so this order is the order of preference there. **That order is the reverse of laws.txt's**: CLawGroup::LoadKey makes each law's node with next = the old head and stores it as the new head (0x5297E5..0x529810), a push to the front. No later reordering was looked for. SetUpCountryLawsAndTechnologyForNewGame walks it too (FINDINGS-starttech.md).
struct_fields.evidence: 0x5297E5 `mov ebx,[edi+0xc]`; operator new(0x10); `mov [eax],esi` (the law); `mov [eax+4],ebx` (next = old head); `mov [edi+0xc],eax` at 0x529810; count +0x10 incremented. What would show it wrong: a pass after loading that reverses or sorts the list - not searched for.

notes: The simulation that checks the reading is in the collecting session's scratchpad, hlB/sim.py (with hlB/techs.py). FINDINGS-ic.md lines 171 and 293 attribute UpdateIC(country, 0) at 0x4D633D to '0x4D59D0'; that call is SetUpCountryForNewGame's, by the same walk-back error.
